base: Each observed statistic is compared with that displaced distribution (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Fig.~\ref*{N-fig:joint5d-nulls}).
Each calibration pseudo-experiment splits the simulation at random into two halves (Table~\ref{tab:joint5d-genmodel}) and refits the background refinement.
Its truth equals $G$ on every fine cell that the source half populates.
Cells it leaves empty lower a coarse cell by at most \SI{0.2}{\percent}, or about \SI{4}{\percent} of the null standard deviation (the per-experiment spread is below \SI{1.5}{\percent} of it).
On the signal, each interaction-model band is renormalized within each fine truth cell, so it moves only the composition within the cell, and with it the efficiency and the migrations.
The flux universe and the band universes are drawn independently, and their weight ratios multiply.
The muon-energy, muon-resolution, and beam-angle lateral bands enter as $\sum_{b}z_{b}\Delta_{b}$, with $\Delta_{b}$ from endpoint unfoldings of the data.
The detector weight bands include the GEANT4 hadron-interaction reweights.
Because the $\Delta_{b}$ come from the observed data, the null distributions are conditional on these data-derived inputs, which would differ in a repeated experiment.
That conditioning has not been validated.

Right: what each element of a pseudo-experiment does, and the corresponding element of the data analysis.
The conditions are numbered (i)--(vi) as in the test specification and grouped into three categories below.
Condition~(i) concerns the null truth below the fine grid.

There it has the Tune~v1 composition of the hypothesis definition (Sec.~\ref{sec:joint5d-design}), varied by the drawn interaction-model universes, with every fine-cell integral held fixed at that of $G$, including the finite-sample fluctuations of $G$'s simulation.
The fine-grid convergence check has not shown convergence.

In the $L_{2}$ norm of the per-cell relative changes, the last refinement, from a twofold-merged grid to the fine grid, is \jtMoneMin--\jtMoneMax{} of the whole change from the coarse test grid to the fine grid.
In that norm the successive refinement changes are therefore not shown to shrink, and the residual below the fine grid is unmeasured and potentially material.
The design assumes that each twofold refinement of the grid multiplies the refinement change, measured in a proxy of the test metric, by a factor of \jtMoneWnormMin--\jtMoneWnormMax{}.
This factor comes from the review of the design, and its derivation is not given.
If the change kept shrinking geometrically at that rate, the residual would be about one to three times the last refinement change, $\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$.
Here $\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$ is the change of the noise-free unfolded result when the null truth is refined from the twofold-merged grid to the fine grid.

That estimate sets the claim variants at $\pm\jtMoneKappa\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$, the central extrapolated estimate, and the robustness variants, for reporting only, at $\pm\jtMoneKappaRobust\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$.
The extrapolation assumes geometric convergence.
The measured $L_{2}$ ratios also allow slower rates and larger residuals.

Measured with $V$ fixed before any observed statistic, the claim variants move the external nulls by \jtMoneClaimSdMin--\jtMoneClaimSdMax{} null standard deviations and the robustness variants by \jtMoneRobSdMin--\jtMoneRobSdMax{}.
For the hybrid null as simulated, the residual plays no role.

The variants carry the rejections over to $G$ itself only if replacing the Tune~v1's shape below the fine grid by $G$'s moves the noise-free unfolded result by no more than $\pm\jtMoneKappa\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$ along $\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$.
Condition~(vi) concerns the predictions' own finite simulated samples, which enter the metric as $\mathrm{diag}\,\mathrm{Var}(\mu_{G})$ and the calibration as a drawn residual term.
The calibration's validity, and what the independent recomputation verifies, are stated in Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d-frozen}.
The analysis bounds two known departures.
Condition~(iv) concerns the simulation size: the pseudo-experiments unfold with half of the simulation and the data with all of it.
The resulting shift $D$, estimated from 16 pairs, is at noise level per cell, with a median $|D|/f$ of 0.02--0.075\%.
Along the null's bias direction it is not always consistent with zero (proxy $a/\mathrm{se}$ of $+4.7$ for the Tune~v1 and $-3.4$ for NuWro), but it is at most 0.068 null standard deviations.
That bound was measured with $V$ fixed before any observed statistic, and it supersedes the specification's estimate of about 0.05.
The shift enters as the bias-aligned upper-bound variant.
That shift was measured for the mean only, in a process without noise or nuisance draws.
A separate check reran the first 200 calibration pseudo-experiments of the NuWro, GENIE~2.12.10, and GENIE~2.12.10 + MEC nulls with a quarter of the simulation.

Between half and quarter simulation, it resolved no change of the null distributions' location, width, or tails: the medians agree within 0.074 null standard deviations, and the widths lie within 0.975--1.010 of the half-simulation values.
The only change it resolved is a mean paired shift of 0.006--0.034 null standard deviations.
Under an assumed extrapolation from half to full simulation that is conservative by design, all three shape decisions, and so all ten, remain rejected.
This check concerns only the simulation size and does not test the data process.
Every pseudo-experiment resamples the same simulated events, so the null distributions are conditional on that simulation.
The decisions closest to their boundary are the shape tests of NuWro and GENIE~2.12.10.

With the Holm order held fixed, their observed statistics exceed the value at which the decision would change by 1.11 and 1.30 null standard deviations, and by 1.01 and 0.67 with the robustness variants at $\pm\jtMoneKappaRobust\,\delta_{\mathrm{fine}}$.
The other eight tests lie 2.7 to 203 null standard deviations from that value, and 2.0 to 203 with the robustness variants.
Crossing that value would make a test undetermined, its Clopper--Pearson interval straddling the threshold, rather than not rejected.
The rounding-level nondeterminism of the data unfolding, measured over the 20 re-unfolds, leaves every observed $p$ value unchanged except NuWro's shape test (2/1752 to 3/1752).
Condition~(ii) concerns the detector model.

Each event uses the simulated detector response, varied only by the drawn detector bands (MINOS muon-matching efficiency and the GEANT4 neutron, pion and proton reweights, each at $\pm1\sigma$) and by the linear surrogate for the five lateral bands.
The surrogate has been checked only for the symmetry of its endpoints.

The analysis's systematic set (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, App.~\ref*{N-app:statmethods}) has no recoil-energy-scale band, so the completeness of the hadronic response is not established (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:joint5d-response}).
Condition~(iii) concerns the interaction-model prior, the analysis's set of \jtModelBands{} interaction-model reweighting bands, with every band drawn in every pseudo-experiment.
Negative weights in two of them, LowQ2\_1 and HighQ2\_1, are clipped per universe.
Measured on the pilot, the effect of clipping them rather than keeping them is at most 0.35\% of a band's shift in whitened norm.
Condition~(v) concerns the neutrino-energy range.

The GiBUU sample contains no events with $E_{\nu}>\SI{20}{GeV}$ (Ref.~\cite{AnalysisNote2026}, Sec.~\ref*{N-sec:eavailw-band}), and its truth outside the test domain ($\pPar\ge\SI{6}{GeV/c}$, with truncated $E_{\nu}$) enters through the migrations into the domain cells.
No prediction contains events with $E_{\nu}>\SI{100}{GeV}$; only the data's flux integral stops there, and the omission is negligible.
The Tune~v1 composition below the fine grid in (i) is also a physical-model assumption.
